headline: New Tech Predicts Floods Sooner Using Satellites and AI
summary: New software combines satellite data with machine learning to give meteorologists advanced warning of deadly flash floods, aiming to save lives.
details: Flash floods are the deadliest weather event globally, and a warming climate is increasing their frequency. New technology, the Transient Artifact and Continuous Learning System (TACLS), is being developed to provide earlier flood warnings.

TACLS uses satellite data and machine learning to analyze conditions and predict areas at risk of flooding. This aims to help the National Weather Service (NWS) issue more timely and accurate flash flood alerts.
Current flood alert systems rely on rain and stream gauges, radar, and human expertise. However, as seen in Lanesville, Indiana, alerts can sometimes come too late, after flooding has already begun.

By integrating advanced analytics, TACLS seeks to streamline the alert process and provide crucial lead time, potentially preventing loss of life and property damage. Scientists hope this system will significantly improve the NWS's ability to protect communities from severe weather.
